:::{#def-translation}
#### Translation

For a fixed vector $\vec{b} \in \reals^m$,
the **translation** by $\vec{b}$ is the function
$t_{\vec{b}} : \reals^m \to \reals^m$ defined by

$$t_{\vec{b}}(\vy) = \vy + \vec{b}$$

It moves every point by the same vector $\vec{b}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-translation}
#### Translating two points

The translation by $\vec{b} = \tp{(1, -2)}$ sends

$$
t_{\vec{b}}\paren{\sbmat{0 \\ 0}} = \sbmat{0 + 1 \\ 0 + (-2)} = \sbmat{1 \\ -2},
\qquad
t_{\vec{b}}\paren{\sbmat{3 \\ 4}} = \sbmat{3 + 1 \\ 4 + (-2)} = \sbmat{4 \\ 2}
$$

Both points move one unit right and two units down.

:::
